items.title: Trump sends envoys to Pakistan for new Iran talks

featured_image.name: Pakistan proposes second round of U.S.-Iran talks as standoff ... - PBS

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Sunday that White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Islamabad for a second round of direct negotiations with Iran, with talks set to begin Tuesday, as the ceasefire between Washington and Tehran approaches its April 22 expiration.[1][2]

In an interview with Fox News, Trump warned that if Tehran does not agree to a deal, the whole of Iran will be "blown up," specifically threatening to target bridges and power plants. He demanded that Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.[2][1]

items.description: A U.S.-backed project in South Africa aims to extract rare earth minerals from massive industrial waste dunes, part of a broader push by Washington to loosen China's grip on the critical minerals supply chain.

items.title: Iran regains 60% of missile launchers during ceasefire, US intelligence estimates

featured_image.name: Iran reportedly recovering bombed missile bunkers within ...

items.description: Seven weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, American intelligence and military officials now estimate that Tehran still holds roughly 60 percent of its pre-war missile launchers and about 40 percent of its long-range attack drone arsenal, according to a report by The New York Times published on Friday. The assessment underscores a widening gap between the Trump administration's claims of having devastated Iran's military and the reality on the ground.[1][2][3]

items.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile into East Sea

featured_image.name: Report: North Korea conducts new missile test from warship - Yahoo

items.description:
North Korea launched at least one ballistic missile eastward on Sunday, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff confirmed, in the latest in a rapid succession of weapons tests that have heightened tensions across the Korean Peninsula this year.[1][2]

The JCS said it detected the missile launch and was analyzing details of the firing, including its range and flight characteristics. The AFP, citing Yonhap, reported that the South Korean military had tracked the missile heading toward the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan.[2][3]

items.description: The war in Iran has pushed the global aviation industry to a breaking point, with jet fuel prices nearly doubling since the conflict began and airlines across Europe, Asia, and North America now canceling flights and grounding aircraft as supplies dwindle.

items.title: Trump Organization plans 70-story tower in Tbilisi, Georgia

featured_image.name: The Trump company is not banning private foreign deals, a break ...

items.description:
The Trump Organization is planning to build a roughly 70-story luxury residential tower in Tbilisi, Georgia, a project that would become the tallest building in the country's capital and mark the family business's latest international venture during Donald Trump's second term in office.

The Wall Street Journal first reported the project on Friday, with Reuters confirming that "Trump Tower Tbilisi" will be a mixed-use development branded by the Trump Organization in partnership with local developers. Details about the specific Georgian partners involved, the project's estimated cost, and its expected timeline have not yet been fully disclosed.[1][2]

items.title: Iran fires on Indian-flag ships after reclosing Hormuz strait

featured_image.name: Firing on Indian ships in Hormuz reveals who wields real power in Iran

items.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reversed the country's decision to reopen the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, reimposing restrictions on the critical waterway and firing on two Indian-flagged vessels attempting to pass through — a sharp escalation that deepened uncertainty over global energy supplies as the 49th day of the U.S.-Iran war drew to a close.
